newsitem.title: GERMANY: Soymeal use lifts 96/97 world oilmeal consumption.
newsitem.headline: Soymeal use lifts 96/97 world oilmeal consumption.

text.p: World consumption of 12 key oilmeals in 1996/97 (Oct/Sept) was forecast at 169.93 million tonnes, up 2.45 million from 95/96, under the lead of soymeal, the independent Oil World newsletter said.
Soymeal would raise its share of use within the group to 53.2 percent from 52.5 percent last season, with total 96/97 use forecast at 90.46 million (87.91 previously).
Consumption of the other 11 meals would be slightly lower than the previous season at 79.47 million tonnes (79.57).
Oil World said most of the rise in soymeal use was due to China, where the expanding red meat and poultry sectors needed raw materials, but other Far Eastern markets were also growing.

By contrast, soymeal and rape meal use in Europe was falling because of high prices and because consumers were able to substitute with cornglutenfeed, sun meal, palmkernel meal, copra meal and fish meal.

Eastern European soymeal demand had also slowed while in the U.S., Oil World expected stagnant figures in April/September after an increase in Oct/March as buyers were expected to shift to cheaper feedgrains.
Oil World also noted rising use of copra and palmkernel meals, groudnut meal and, to a lesser extent, fish meal.
